lessons.name: transfer
lessons.note: `s`, `t` and `n` on the outer keys, and `e` and `i` on the inner, are Dosh's own keys and mean the same here.  Add `Bk`, the space thumb, to a vowel to end the word.  Also the two commands with nothing to learn: right `Bk` alone is a space, and the whole left outer row is undo.
lessons.title: what transfers from Dosh

lessons.name: vowels
lessons.note: The three vowels Dosh does not give away, and the three sharpest conflicts on the board: `a` is the `Sp` thumb alone, which is Backspace in Dosh; `o` is `e+i`, Dosh's one-shot shift; `u` is `i+Sp`, Dosh's full stop.  Plus `Bk` to end the word.  They come second because almost no English word can be spelled without them, so every consonant lesson after this one drills its shape on ordinary words.
lessons.title: the vowels a, o and u

lessons.name: r
lessons.note: Dosh types `a` here.
lessons.title: r on the pinky

lessons.name: c
lessons.note: Dosh types `o` here.
lessons.title: c on the lower ring

lessons.name: d
lessons.note: Dosh types `q` here.
lessons.title: d is t plus the pinky

lessons.name: p
lessons.note: Dosh has one-shot alt here.
lessons.title: p on the ring pair

lessons.name: f
lessons.note: Dosh types `u` here.
lessons.title: f on lower ring and middle

lessons.name: y
lessons.note: Dosh types `j` here.
lessons.title: y on pinky and upper middle

lessons.name: th
lessons.note: Dosh types `g` here.
lessons.title: th on lower ring and upper middle

lessons.name: l
lessons.note: Dosh types `?` here.
lessons.title: l on upper ring and lower middle

lessons.name: b
lessons.note: Dosh has one-shot gui here.
lessons.title: b is p plus the pinky

lessons.name: w
lessons.note: Dosh types `p` here.
lessons.title: w on the upper ring and middle

lessons.name: g
lessons.note: Dosh types `l` here.
lessons.title: g is c plus the pinky

lessons.name: h-st
lessons.note: The one shape that reads differently on the two hands.  Dosh has one-shot control here.
lessons.title: h as an onset, st as a coda

lessons.name: x
lessons.note: Dosh has PrintScreen here.
lessons.title: x on the middle pair and lower ring

lessons.name: second-r-l
lessons.note: The left hand's inner four are the second character of the syllable, mostly consonants.  `r` is `Bk` alone and `l` is `Sp` alone.
lessons.title: the second character: r and l

lessons.name: second-i-t-m
lessons.note: `i` is the same key as the vowel; `t` is `e+Sp`, `m` is `e+Bk`.
lessons.title: the second character: i, t and m

lessons.name: second-o-s-e
lessons.note: `o` is `e+i` as for the vowel; `s` is `e` alone; `e` is `i+Bk`.
lessons.title: the second character: o, s and e

lessons.name: second-rest
lessons.note: `w` is `Sp+Bk`, `c` is `e+i+Sp`, `u` is `i+Sp` as for the vowel, `p` is `e+i+Bk`, `n` is `e+Sp+Bk`.
lessons.title: the second character: w, c, u, p and n

lessons.name: ea-ou
lessons.note: `ea` is `e+Sp` (e plus a); `ou` is `e+i+Sp+Bk` (o plus u), and only ever ends a word.  These are the free combinations: they spell the digraph only with a second character, which is why they come after those; `ea` alone is a placeholder glyph.
lessons.title: ea and ou

lessons.name: v-m-k
lessons.note: Free in Dosh: nothing to unlearn.  `v` is f plus the pinky.
lessons.title: v, m and k

lessons.name: nd-ng-nt
lessons.note: Three-key shapes that spell a whole cluster: `ind`, `inc` and `int` as onsets, `nd`, `ng` and `nt` as codas.
lessons.title: ind/nd, inc/ng and int/nt

lessons.name: ch-sh-gh-z-ck
lessons.note: `sh` is ch plus the pinky; `z` is s plus the pinky.
lessons.title: ch, sh, gh, z and ck

lessons.name: coda-h-e
lessons.note: Two four-key right-hand shapes with no onset reading: a final `h` and a final `e`.
lessons.title: the coda-only shapes: h and e

lessons.name: silent-e
lessons.note: With no vowel on the right hand and a real coda, a second character that is also a vowel supplies the nucleus, and the stroke appends a silent `e` and ends the word: `time`, `tone`, `tame`.
lessons.title: the mirrored vowel and the silent e

lessons.name: clusters
lessons.note: An onset and a second character that spell a cluster together: `h+r` is `str`, `h+l` is `spl`, `h+p` is `spr`, `h+c` is `scr`, `sh+c` is `sch`, `z+c` is `sk`, `s+s` is `sci`, `y+i` is `j`, `c+c` is `qu`.
lessons.title: the onset clusters

lessons.name: h-after-p-w-r
lessons.note: The second character `w` (`Sp+Bk`) spells `h` after an onset ending in `p`, `w` or `r`: `ph`, `wh`, `rh`.
lessons.title: w reads as h after p, w and r

lessons.name: diphthongs
lessons.note: A second-character `u` before the vowel `u` spells `au`, and `i` before `i` spells `ai`.
lessons.title: au and ai

lessons.name: final-y
lessons.note: `y` as a coda with the `i`-ending vowel keys spells just `y` and ends the word: the `ui` keys give the space and nothing else.
lessons.title: a bare final y
